title: Larry, Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office
hook: A rescue tabby from Battersea has outlasted a string of prime ministers.
peek: Larry is the cat who lives at 10 Downing Street. He arrived from a London rescue centre in 2011, and because he belongs to the staff rather than the prime minister, he stays while governments come and go.
lede: In February 2011, a brown and white tabby from Battersea Dogs and Cats Home moved into 10 Downing Street. Larry was given the title Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office, the first cat to hold it officially. He belongs to the civil service staff rather than to any prime minister, so when leaders move out, Larry stays.

bullets.text: Larry came from Battersea Dogs and Cats Home, the London rescue centre founded in the 1860s. Staff there reportedly picked him for his keen hunting instinct, which made his adoption one of the best-known in Britain.

The government's own website describes his duties as greeting guests, inspecting security defences and testing antique furniture for napping quality. He is said to be wary of strangers, despite spending his days on a doorstep full of cameras.

Larry arrived under David Cameron and has stayed through Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak, Keir Starmer and, from July 2026, Andy Burnham. He has become a fixture of news footage outside the famous black door.
From 2016 the Foreign Office next door had its own Battersea cat, Palmerston. Newspapers covered his standoffs with Larry on Downing Street with mock seriousness until Palmerston retired in 2020.
